utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone in this courtroom. The parties have received a copy of the decision that was filed, decision on the motion to dismiss under Article 98 bis. And since this decision only partially grants the motion in respect of three sniping incidents, this means that the time has come now for the Defence to present its case. Although we have some practical issues to discuss rather soon, I would first like to give the opportunity to the Defence to make a statement at the beginning of the presentation of its case. And as far as I understand, you have divided your job, and part of it will -- of the statement will be given by Ms. Pilipovic, and part of it will be given by Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Who may I given an opportunity first to start with your statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon to all those in the courtroom. Your Honours, at the moment when the Defence in conformity with Rule 84 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence is beginning its case and with its opening statement, we already have behind us over 13.000 pages of transcript, including the evidence of more than 100 witnesses for the Prosecution before this Court, and a great deal of written and other evidence which the Prosecution used desires of proving its claims set out in the indictment charging General Stanislav Galic that from about the 10th of September until about August 1994, he engaged in the long lasting campaign of shelling and sniping of the civilian population and civilian targets, from which the Prosecutor in points 1 to 7 draws a legal conclusion that General Stanislav Galic was responsible for the terrorist acts against civilians in violation of Article 51 of the additional protocol 1 and Article 13 of the additional protocol 2 of the Geneva Conventions of 1949 and which are sanctionable under Article 3 of the Statute of Tribunal and then murder sanctionable under 5(A) of the Statute and inhumane acts which are not a murder sanctionable under Article 5(i) of the statute. According to the Prosecution, the SRC for 44 months conducted this campaign in order to murder, mutilate, wound, and terrorize the civilian population. The Prosecutor even goes as far as to say inappropriately and groundlessly that the recent history is not aware of such a campaign, the purpose of which was to take a population back into the conditions of the Middle Ages. The Prosecutor has not proved existence of any campaign, and especially not a campaign, the purpose of which would be to take a population back to the medieval conditions. Every war carries certain difficulties and under conditions of urban warfare, one cannot request conditions that reign in peace. The Prosecutor claims that the former Yugoslav People's Army took strategic positions in and around Sarajevo, that the city was blocked after that, and as the colloquialism goes, that it was held under siege and thus acquired all the elements of a famed before the eyes of the world public opinion and that they did all that with the participation of the JNA. The Defence will produce evidence to show that none of this is true and will not allow media forgeries to remain unclarified and to affect the decision of the Trial Chamber. Unbiased observers could see that only the Yugoslav People's Army could prevent a war between the parties to the war as claimed, among others, by Mr. Cyrus Vance. The withdraw of the Yugoslav People's Army provide the conditions for the commencement of war operations of Muslim forces which, for the duration of the war, set out to prolong the war violating regularly even all the initial agreements, some cease fires, in their desire of internationalising the war. The Defence would like now to show tape MFI number 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you inform that the numbering of the tapes to be shown has been arranged with the Registrar, so we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Many examples clearly illustrate the media campaign against the Serbs during the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is, in the Sarajevo theatre of war. This campaign was not routed in facts and was based on invented events and forged facts as will be clearly shown in the video material which we shall see later on. Unfortunately the truth about the dirty media war resorted to by the political and military leadership of Bosnia-Herzegovina can -- has -- is surfacing today still with great difficulty. The Defence hopes that the Trial Chamber will see from the evidence which will be produced that there was a great deal of untruth in many reports and that the public was reached only by the truth which the Bosnia-Herzegovina side wanted it to see, and that even the official UN reports were either glossed over or even incorrect. From the very onset, the Serbs were proclaimed aggressors even though it was unclear how the war started, and that the murder of member of a wedding party was then introduction to the war. The media manipulation went on. The term notion of ethnic cleansing was invented. It was claimed that only Serbs were engaging in it, and a black and white picture was being created about good and bad guys, a picture that there had been no Serbs in Bosnia, although, as a matter of fact, Serbs have been living there for centuries and own 70 per cent of its territory. Concocted and done up pictures of events are used and they are placed through press services so that the journalists don't even know what really goes on because they never even went to that part of Sarajevo which was under the Serb control. On the other hand, the media glossed over evident crimes in Bosnia committed against Serbs. All this contributed to creating an erroneous image on the events in Bosnia and Sarajevo. Could we now have a tape, MFI-19.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor set out to present a simplified and distorted portrait of the causes of the conflict, taking out only the conflict in and around Sarajevo, which until then, lived an orderly multi-ethnic life seemingly without a danger to suffer the same fate as Slovenia and Croatia; transcript 563. The Prosecutor claims that peace ended on the 6th of April when the European Community recognized the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the beginning, that is in the beginning of April 1992, when the inhabitants of Sarajevo saw the Yugoslav People's Army forces engage in drills around Sarajevo. The Defence will prove that peace in Sarajevo and Bosnia was threatened and brought into question much earlier during the significant preparations of Muslim paramilitary forces formed on the -- formed as the units of a party army, that is the militant wing of the SDA. The Prosecutor turn as blind eye to the fact that Mr. Sefer Halilovic in his book, "The Cunning Strategy," presented clear information that the Green Berets led to the creation of the Patriotic League as early at 1991. And that by 1992, they had already covered with the armed detachments, headed by men with a significant criminal record, the whole city and even Bosnia, so that by April 1992 they already had a Muslim paramilitary para-army in existence, which at that time, was 150 men strong. Now the question arises as to who and why needed that army. According to Sefer Halilovic on the 7th and 8th of February, 1992, a military meeting was held in a village of Mehuric, Evna [phoen], Travnik which drew out the plans for municipalities and regions on the basis of which attacks were to be prepared against the Yugoslav People's Army which, according to the already known scenario, was to be proclaimed an aggressor army. Alija Izetbegovic's party army was to ensure the takeover of power and is remaining the head of state. But not a state which would be also the state of Croats and Serbs as until that time, but a Muslim state only, in which there would only be room for those who accept to live in accordance with the rules of an insignificant Muslim majority. All of this takes place without the knowledge of Serbs, who were caught unaware by the accommodations of the SDA, that is Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, that a Muslim young man should not report to summons for their military service; and the activities of the SDA leadership to dismiss the staff of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina; and appoint to the leading post a man loyal to the SDA, that is, Party of Democratic Action, which to all intents and purposes started the disintegration of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina into its Muslim and its Serb part. The Defence will call expert witnesses to prove that it is indispensable to look at the historical, constitutional, and the military side of the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina so as to fully understand how the division of Sarajevo came about and how further developments unfolded which doubtlessly were quite different in nature than affirmed by the Prosecution. The Prosecutor tried through the expert witness Robert Donia to present the causes of the political division of the city of Sarajevo. But this expert produced a completely wrong opinion and to put together a construct which has no basis in real events. This expert wrongly claims and produces no argument to prove his thesis that the campaign of the original organisation undertaken by the SDS was the cause, was the root, of all the divisions in Bosnia and Herzegovina and Sarajevo. This expert alleges that the SDS leaders undertook the confirmation of the government -- of the rule of that party in the largest territory possible, and they also undertook to separate that territory from the effective control of the republican authority. This expert at the same time does not say that according to the constitutional provisions of the then valid constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina regarding the decision making on the matters of importance for the quality of all three peoples, that is, Serbs, Croats, and Muslims. The decision making prescribed was such as to preclude the overvoting by any people. And nevertheless the most important decision, the decision on the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Muslims and Croats took by overvoting the Serbs and in a procedure which violated the manner of decision making in the Assembly which envisaged -- which envisaged decision making by consensus. The decision was adopted at the session of the Assembly held between the 11th and the 15th of October in the form of a memorandum on the sovereignty of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and threatened with using the Serb people to an ethnic minority. At that time, at that moment, the representatives of the Serb people in accordance with amendment 70 to paragraph 10 to the constitution of the BH asked for this decision to be taken to the council for national equality to be assessed. And after that, the President of the Assembly, Mr. Momcilo Krajisnik concluded the Assembly session for that day. However, the representatives of the Muslim and Croatian parties illegally and unconstitutionally continued to work in the Assembly without the presence of Serb representatives in the Assembly and they adopted the aforementioned decision. The response to such behaviour of the representatives of the Muslims and Croats was to establish the authorities of the -- organs of authorities in the municipalities where the Serbs had the majority. This way of organising of the Serb people represents practically a political division of the city of Sarajevo and represents the cessation of work of joint organs on all levels, which later represented the basis for the -- also for the territorial division of the city of Sarajevo and for the regionalisation, which according to the constitutional provisions was carried out legally. The Prosecutor says that on the 7th of April, 1992, the Serbs declared the Serbian Republic of BH which was known from August 1992 as Republika Srpska in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and they demanded the majority of the territory of that republic. Transcript page 563: "The Serbian people starting from the right to self-determination brought a decision to establish their state and they did not ask for the majority of the territory of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina because they did not have anyone to ask it from, because they already had the majority of the territory." As we had seen it earlier on the video, because according to the Cadastre information more than 70 per cent of land was owned by Serbs. The Prosecutor claims that the objective of Republika Srpska in relation to Sarajevo became very clear after the Assembly of the Serbian people was held on the 12th of May 1992. And that it was on that day that the army of Republika Srpska was created, which effectively transformed the JNA units that had been left over and other units that were loyal to Republika Srpska. And that became the command -- becoming under the -- being under command on the of Republika Srpska and that such army was later opposed to the government of the BH which then later became the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It is true that it was on the 12th of May, 1992, that the Republika Srpska Assembly was held, and that it was on that Assembly that the objectives of Republika Srpska were set out. That Assembly, as far as Sarajevo is concerned, the Republika Srpska decided that just like the Muslim side, Sarajevo -- to declare Sarajevo as its capital city, because about 180.000 Serbs lived in Sarajevo, considering the historic, ethnic, and ownership right on the land in the city of Sarajevo. The Serbs were well grounded in their beliefs that they had a part of that city as their own. However, it is not true, which will be proved by the Defence, that the army of Republika Srpska was created from the leftover units of the JNA and other units that were loyal to Republika Srpska. Because it is completely clear that by the withdrawal of the former JNA, any JNA units ceased to exist and on the territory of Sarajevo at that time, there were units that were established that divided -- divided the Territorial Defence from the local population which later became army of Republika Srpska. Bearing in mind this fact, and the right to live in the city where their families lived for several centuries back, the Serbs had decided to defend their parts of the city. The Defence will, therefore, prove that Sarajevo as a city was neither under siege nor blocked, nor was there any plan to expose its inhabitants to terror, but that it became divided city by ethnic lines. With the first barricades that were set up and following the event in Bascarsija of the 1st of March, 1992, which was an introduction to the conflict in Sarajevo, as we saw it earlier on the video, the demarcation lines were established in the city of Sarajevo, which followed the line of majority ethnic division. And that these lines, by the units of the Territorial Defence linking themselves, which were on the Serb side, defended their own territory under the command of the VRS. They then became demarcation lines between warring parties, and as such, became the lines of the division of the city of Sarajevo. These lines were not significantly moved throughout the war, except for small changes which brought tactical improvements of both sides. The Defence will prove that this was a legitimate right that the Serbs had which was confirmed apart from what the Serb side did by the Dayton Agreement, by which the Republika Srpska was recognised as well as Srpska Sarajevo as a city. The Prosecutor claims that after that there were clashes between the BH army and the VRS, and that the two armies fought in a pact position, because the demarcation lines stayed static, and that neither side could deliver the coup de gras. This was page 564 of the transcript. The Prosecutor says that the BH army of the 1st Corps of the BH army had about 75.000 soldiers which were engaged in combat, while the Sarajevo Romanija Corps had only 18.000 soldiers. The Prosecutor further claims that the SRK had all the high points around Sarajevo and that it had far more artillery, which is why the BH army had also an advantage in troops, while the SRK had an advantage in weapons and materiel. The only true facts from these allegations of the Prosecutor, Defence can only accept the numerical situation because all the facts say that the BH 1st Corps had 75.000 soldiers out of which 40.000 in the city itself, while the Sarajevo Romanija Corps had about 18.000 soldiers around the entire front line which was 237 kilometres in length. All other allegations of the Prosecutor are unfounded. The taking of Sarajevo was not planned because the Serb side believed that the Sarajevo should be divided, which happened. Serb side had an advantage in heavy weaponry but did not have much more or significantly more artillery, which is what the Prosecutor says, because the facts will show that it only had a relative advantage in the -- in the numbers of artillery pieces which, in the conditions of urban warfare, it doesn't have a real advantage -- doesn't give a real advantage. It is not true what the Prosecutor claims, that the SRK took up all domineering high points around Sarajevo. The Defence will prove that the 1st Corps of the BH army throughout the conflict had the control of the Grdonj hill, the area of Seven Woods or Sedam Suma, Hum Hill, Zuc, Mount Igman, Mojmilo hill, Vezika and Mala, Colina Kapa, and Debezo hill, from which positions they controlled all the positions of Serb forces and the entire city of Sarajevo. Taking into consideration that the 1st Corps controlled most of Dobrinja, Vojnicko Polje, Alipasino Polje, Cengic Vila, Marin Dvor, that is, parts of the city where the highest buildings were built, from which most of them, a majority of them were used for military purposes to place sniper nests, machine-gun nests, for command units of the 1st Corps. Then it is perfectly clear, which will also be proven in fact, that the VRS, that is the SRK, did not have such tactical positions which would enable them to have tactical and military advantage, but it was the other way around. The advantage of the control of the high points in Sarajevo was had by the units of the 1st Corps, and that is how they had considerable operative advantage over the forces of the VRS. The forces of the SRK, therefore, were forced to use artillery and that exclusively against military targets. And after the units of the 1st Corps of the BH carried out operations by responding to these operations in order to realise the military objective to keep 75.000 soldiers of the BH army in and around Sarajevo. Because the opposite happened, such a large number of troops leaving the Sarajevo theatre, would mean the defeat of the VRS. The Prosecutor claims that during the conflict, there were legitimate military actions in Sarajevo. And still, the Prosecutor claims that there was a campaign that was conducted of deliberately sniping and terrorising civilians, although, the shelling was sometimes used to hit certain civilians, and in other cases, that the civilians were targeted in a random manner. Transcript 568: "The evidence of the Defence will prove that this viewpoint of the Prosecutor is unfounded and that during the presentation of his case, the Prosecutor was not able to prove which illegitimate military actions they were, as opposed to legitimate actions, considering that there was war in Sarajevo, and daily combat, daily battles." The Prosecutor had to make a distinction between legitimate and illegitimate actions, to clearly delineate which actions were illegitimate in order to appreciate what he has actually proved. The Defence will prove that the Sarajevo theatre was a theatre of urban war, that the demarcation lines went through the city, and that the two armies were divided just by a street just by one street or by the Miljacka river, with a very narrow bed or that they were divided by one building. And they were such positions that both armies were in one same building all around a facility, which is for instance, the stadium of the football club Zeljeznicar or the Jewish cemetery. The Defence would like this photograph MFI-25 to be placed on the ELMO, please. This building that we can see on the ELMO is located in Grbavica. And around this building there were fierce clashes because both sides had its positions, their positions, in it. So occasionally, they were just divided by a wall. And we will come back to this later in the presentation of our evidence. During combat for these buildings hundreds of bullets could have gone to undesirable directions and causing undesirable consequences. The photograph is no longer needed. Thank you. Bearing in mind that the 1st Corps of the BH army had about 40.000 armed troops, and about 15.000 policemen in Sarajevo. The evidence of the Defence will prove that in order for such a large number of troops to function, there was a lot of accommodation that was needed. And a considerable and important number of facilities for command posts were needed, so that at any given point in the city, there were over 1.000 legitimate military targets, that could have been targeted at any time. The majority of such military targets were positioned in what previously were civilian facilities. As an example, we will give you the command post of the 6th Mountain Brigade in a residential building in the street of Ivana Krndelja in Hrasno. The command post of the 2nd Motorised Brigade in the student halls in Nedzarici. Command of the Sultan Fatih Brigade of the building of the former Medresa Muslim school for women near the political science faculty, command post of the Mahima Pustalija [phoen] Brigade in the primary school in Bistrik, and many, many other locations that will be mentioned in the testimony of the Defence witnesses. While the command of the 1st Corps did not respect the provisions of Article 58 of the Additional Protocol I that make it a duty to remove civilian population near military facilities and from the locations of military operations. Bearing in mind the position of legitimate military targets an expectation of the other side, that is, the command of the 1st Corps of BG will remove the civilians from the areas of war operations and that it will not place military facilities in civilian buildings. Practically there was no area in the city which could be [as interpreted] considered as a legitimate military target, bearing in mind in the area of probable errors, then the claim of the Prosecutor that the civilians and civilian facilities were deliberately targeted is completely unacceptable, just like the position of the Prosecutor that there was unselected or random targeting, also unacceptable. In such conditions of urban warfare during which BH army often used the so-called mobile mortars, as well as other artillery weapons, which had to have returned fire from heavy weapons in order to stop the military actions of the other side. It is hard to speak about the application, the principle of distinction, because it has already been said. This was very difficult to enforce because of the behaviour of the political and military leadership of the BH which did not respect the conditions of warfare by using in an authorised manner, and in violation of Geneva Conventions, civilian facilities and preparation of carrying out military actions. The Defence would like to also point here to the unfounded allegations of the Prosecutor that General Galic could be responsible for the excessive use of force. The 1st Corps of the BH had at its disposal, as it was said, a good number of artillery pieces, artillery weapons, which were used to carry out direct attacks on the VRS positions, and which were cleverly distributed throughout the city which were very frequently, and almost on a daily basis, used as extremely movable mobile fire points very frequently near or from the immediate vicinity of various objects, cultural and historical monuments, medical institutions and similar locations. And the evidence will prove that this was done in a deliberate fashion so that these positions would draw return fire of the SRK units, and then create a picture in the media that the VRS is attacking civilian facilities, even hospitals, which was well-known by the commanders of the UN forces. But for different reasons, they did not publicise this, which created a false picture on the crimes committed by Serbs, which we will see from what Lord Owen said in a video in relation to the behaviour of General Morillon whose letter is mentioned. And the Defence has already proposed it as evidence, and this is already in the file. I would now ask for the videotape MFI-20, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By using artillery weapons and light mortars, including 82-millimetre calibre mortars, units of the 1st Corps of the BH army also supported the infantry operations. And it is completely clear that such operations were responded by the fire from adequate weapons by the SRK units. In such conditions of continual mutual exchange of fire throughout the Sarajevo theatre which should be assessed according to the rules of military of the art of war, because the logistic forces for supporting the troops logistically on the first front line were certainly billeted in the back. So what happened is because the civilian population were not removed from the area of combat as this was explained by the witness who was the commander of the 1st Corps, what happened was that civilians were killed, but not to an extent at that time it was presented in the media. This happened because of possible collateral errors and also because civilians and in an unauthorised way and in their own will, regardless of their safety, they stayed and remained in the area of combat operations. The Defence evidence will prove that the units of the SRK did not have an order to carry out operations against any civilian target, that civilian targets were not deliberately targeted, and that so far what the Prosecutor has shown as evidence is not -- is not reliable. The killing of civilians which happened cannot be a result of the following. It could be the consequences of the exchange of fire in the conditions of urban warfare because of the authorised command of the units of the SRK. And their assessment was that in certain operations, possibly there were some small civilian casualties which, in comparison with the military advantage which was accepted, were insignificant, bearing in mind that it was illegitimate, illegal, to keep the civilians in this area as provided for in the Geneva Conventions. The operations that were undertaken as a response to the commenced offensive operations of the BiH were undertaken in a legitimate manner, and the Prosecutor has not shown in a single example, for instance, in shelling, that the civilian population was killed, except the Prosecutor claims that this happened in five selected incidents about which we will speak later. So we cannot speak here about any omissions on the side of the command of the units of the SRK; and least of all by General Galic who, as the evidence will show, asked from his units absolutely to respect all the laws and customs of war. General Galic never received a single protest in relation to individual sniper incidents on the basis of which he would be able to carry out a detailed investigation to see who from which positions, which objective, opened fire. The claim of the Prosecutor that the units and the individuals of the SRK acted in a deliberate manner against civilians is unacceptable. And it is even less acceptable to say that this was a campaign against civilians, deliberate killings, or rather inhumane acts that are not murders. The evidence presented by the Prosecution has already shown that the BH army was equipped with sniping weapons to such an extent that it enjoyed considerable advantage, both in terms of the number and quality of sniping weapons, and also in terms of locations of sniper nests or snipers' positions. When this is added, the fact that sniping units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were deployed at all levels of the military organisation and that some of them were under the direct command of the -- of corps commander or under the command of -- commander of special police forces, then evidently the army of Republika Srpska had to address this problem seriously. And this led to the establishment of entire sniping units at a later stage of the conflict because before that attempt notwithstanding it was not possible to respond adequately to the organised actions of ABiH snipers formed to fight against the snipers of the ABiH, rather than to attack -- to target civilians. The Prosecution's evidence produced in order to confirm so-called distributed sniper incidents, and that the Defence evidence that will be produced during our case will clearly show that none of these incidents happened in a manner described by the Prosecution. At this moment, we also have your decision regarding the motion of the Defence for an acquittal. After the presentation of the Prosecution case, you decided that for the incidents under numbers 7, 12, and 19, the Prosecutor has not produced evidence beyond any reasonable doubt that General Galic could be criminally charged. This means that in the further course of this case, it is necessary for the Defence to show that even in the remaining 23 incidents do not contain any elements that would produce facts indicative of General Galic's responsibility. The evidence produced by the Defence will show that there is absolutely no serious parameter to justify the Prosecution's allegations that the civilians were targeted deliberately. None of them saw the place where the bullets were fired from. They were unable to indicate the true direction of the fire. Some of these events are an obvious example of so-called ricochet, and all the other incidents are obvious examples of the so-called stray bullet effect. The Defence will prove that all the injured were in the area of the exchange of fire, and that accidental injuries were a possibility. The Defence will prove that it was physically impossible to act from individual areas where the soldiers of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps were, that they were not able to act from those areas against those parts of the city where, as the Prosecution alleges, victims were injured. The Prosecution's allegations that the profession, age, gender, and ethnic origin were not of importance for snipers, that children were hit as they were playing -- even as they were playing in their gardens, or people who were in their flats, or as they were collecting firewood or crossing the street, taking water from a canal. With all due respect for the victims of the armed conflict, all these allegations show that the Prosecution has fallen under the influence of the earlier media campaign which endeavored to, at all costs, show the world that the Serb troops were doing none other but targeting civilians. And in all this it is forgotten that it was wartime, that in wartime conditions when there is daily fighting, people cannot behave as they would in peace, to walk around with friends or children, to chat in the streets, and move where and when they want. War means rules which concentrate not only media participants in the events and force people to behave in a certain matter, but even more so in personal constraints on the civilian population which must be removed from the area of combat operations, because if they remain -- whenever they remain in that area, they are under threat. The Prosecutor has even failed to show that the remaining 23 scheduled incidents happened in precisely that manner, that is, that these people were targeted deliberately and have proven even less that the person who fired could know whether it was a Serb, a Muslim, or somebody. Transcript 567. Quite simply, civilians were never targeted deliberately and the circumstances under which the 23 incidents happened, and we need to produce further evidence about them, show an absence of intent to use direct fire against them. The number of the injured and killed inhabitants of Sarajevo is far from being such as presented by the authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina and representatives of some media and accepted without a reservation, or perhaps because they accepted it intending to side with the Muslim party. And unfortunately the Prosecution has also accepted these figures claiming that in Sarajevo there were thousands of dead and wounded. Figures are subject of such manipulation. Can we have MFI-21 played, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence will show by using statistical methods different from those which were used by an expert of the Prosecution, the expert which is an employee of the Prosecutor's office. And the Defence finds this unacceptable. We will show, therefore, by applying other statistical matters that the figures which are given cannot be termed as thousands of injured and dead in Sarajevo in themselves, as the Prosecutor says. And the Prosecutor thus, by accepting this -- these figures, follows the line of uncorroborated claims in the media which were manipulated at the expense of the Serb forces during the conflict. The data processing method concerning the number of victims in relation to the overall number of inhabitants in Sarajevo at the moment of war will show that the number of casualties or fatalities is a figure which may not be considered the effect, the result, the product, of the campaign of the deliberate targeting of civilians. The Defence considers that the evidence it will bring forward will show that the Prosecution's claim about the existence of a sniping campaign is an unacceptable claim, even if one accepts that the 23 scheduled incidents are illustrations of how civilians suffered and fell victim to firearms that - again, even if it were accepted, would not be approved - which could confirm the existence of a campaign beyond a reasonable doubt. Generalized claims of the Prosecution that these are merely examples and that they existed also at other times and in other places cannot be accepted because the Prosecutor needs to prove the existence of every fact, that is, he must prove that somebody was injured, what he was injured by, where he was injured, what were the circumstances under which he was injured, and all of this is still under a very serious question mark. The Defence will show that the Prosecutor was unable to prove it, and that therefore his claim that there was a campaign to use snipers against civilians will be unacceptable. At the time when the events took place, the intervals between incidents, different places where these events took place as described in 23 so-called scheduled incidents in annex 1 to the indictment can in no way be a foundation for proving a campaign. A campaign presumes proven, frequent, if not daily incidents, then incidents which happen at certain places in large numbers in order to prove the action of snipers and firm proof that the incidents happened because bullets were fired from the positions of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. This Trial Chamber, for the time being, does not have such evidence at its disposal, and the Defence believes that the existence of the campaign will not be acceptable after the Defence produces its evidence. By creating a simplified picture of the sniper actions and by proclaiming that sniper -- by proclaiming every action from firearms of small calibre as sniper actions, and including anti-aircraft guns and mortars, the Prosecution wishes, realising that it is unable to prove that the civilians were deliberately targeted by snipers, to ensure for itself a broader field for such claims. The Defence believes so that such an approach is wrong and that the term "sniping" as used by the Prosecution may not be accepted as the Defence will show, hoping that at the end of the -- of our case, the Trial Chamber will also change its attitude regarding the term of "sniping." The Defence will call ballistics experts to define clearly the difference between sniping and the use of other fire weapons, because it is indispensable to assess under what conditions and at which places one can speak about possible sniping actions and when that is not possible. And all this will be of great use, of great benefit, to the Trial Chamber to draw its conclusions as to whether the Prosecutor has proven his allegations about the existence of a campaign of the targeting of civilians and the deliberate murdering -- killing of civilians. The Defence deems that its evidence will show that the conclusion in the above sense is impossible. The question of the conduct of members of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps conducive to the deliberate killing of civilians which could be qualified as crimes of murder, in terms of facts, cannot be accepted because the Defence will show that there was no intent to kill civilians. Such a conclusion will become inevitable after all the circumstances are -- under which certain incidents took place are assessed, and especially regarding the possibility to establish the direction from which the bullet has arrived. And all the contradictions in the statements of the witnesses for the Prosecution will be particularly taken care of. To establish an intent, it is not -- it is not sufficient for the Prosecutor to refer to the statements of some witnesses, that they were the targets of snipers. First and foremost, it must be -- the facts must be established showing beyond any reasonable doubt that the one who was firing a bullet at that particular moment had the intention to kill precisely that particular civilian. The question of intent may not be established on the basis of witnesses' conclusions who do not know who is firing, where he is firing from, or why he is firing a bullet. The Defence will, therefore, produce evidence to show that there were exchanges of fire and possible accidental civilian casualties, if, that is, one can say that persons who find themselves in the area of the combat activities may be considered as civilians. Because the evidence produced so far has shown that soldiers wore civilian clothes, and that therefore it was impossible to tell them apart from civilians, especially bearing in mind the distance between the alleged victim and the one who is allegedly firing shots, and the equipment and type of the weapon being fired. The Defence will also show that the firing -- that the members of the units of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps did not open fire intending to injure any civilian or such injuries that would represent other inhumane acts, as the Prosecution claims. So the Prosecution will set out to show in the course of its case that there was no plan to use sniping fire against civilians, and that General Galic never ever ordered anyone to open fire on civilians, that General Galic never ever received a protest indicative of wrongful action of any member of units under his command, and in particular, that he was never ever informed that any civilian fell victim during an individual incident. The Defence will set out to show that General Galic had no knowledge of any wrongful conduct of members of his units that would prompt him to launch an investigation if it was conduct which was subject to disciplinary liability. Or in case of a doubt that the crime had been committed, he did not require any investigation because it was not his responsibility in such cases to undertake anything. All that he was responsible for was to request that an investigation be launched and conducted by relevant bodies of the military judiciary. In all this, one must bear in mind that General Galic holds the 4th degree of command in relation to soldiers. We shall set out to prove that General Galic, apart from general orders that civilian objects may not be targeted - and these were the orders that he regularly issued - he as a Corps Commander could not issue any other orders, and that he had no information that his orders were not being obeyed, and that even if he received such information he always took measures, took steps, to have that information verified. The Defence will set out to prove that General Galic, even when he requested the verification of certain formation, invariably received the answer that there was no actions undertaken either by units or individuals necessitating further investigation. It is quite clear that under such circumstances, General Galic was not nor could be criminally responsible for any act that he is charged with in the indictment in relation to sniping actions, either under provisions of Article 7(1) or of provisions of 7(3) under the Statute of the Trial Chamber. The indictment charges General Galic with the same crimes committed at the same time, but with the use -- but through the use of weapons which use shells or mines, in direct or indirect fire, and as an illustration the Prosecutor showed -- illustrated only five incidents caused by mortar fire. That factor itself shows that the Prosecutor has produced no evidence that members of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps opened fire, according to our military doctrine, that are used for direct fire from guns or tanks. And that the only conclusion one can draw from it is that these weapons were not engaged in any illegitimate military action. Your decision, Your Honours, adopted following the Defence motion in line with Rule 98 bis, it was passed from your decision that you believe that the Prosecutor has produced enough evidence, if it were to be admitted, to produce a sufficient body of facts for conviction in relation to scheduled shelling incidents. The Defence will, in its case, produce evidence to refute even that meager evidence which the Prosecutor has produced to convict General Galic for incidents described in five scheduled shelling incidents. The Defence has hired an expert team of the highest scientific and military rank who will scientifically and with a large number of empirical examples refute every Prosecutor's claim concerning the firing of mortar mines from the positions of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, and who will especially deny the generalized and unfounded claims of the Prosecution's expert witnesses who voiced their opinions without a single scientific fact. We shall show you a graph, MFI-26.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC

With the objective of the propaganda and the psychological war that was conducted by the Muslim authorities, they staged other incidents - and also at the time when important political events were held - with the objective of representing the Serbs in the least favourable light. utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Through its evidence, the Defence will show that the other scheduled incidents of shelling were also not caused by SRK units. Looking at everything the Defence will offer as evidence it is certain that the claim of the Prosecutor could be accepted, that General Galic could be criminally and legally responsible in relation to shelling, neither by Article 7(1) or by commander responsibility of Article 7(3) of the Statute. In all his aspects of his command, General Galic strictly applied the rules, and he did not fail to take measures that his duty implied, bearing in mind his position in that system of command. There isn't a single document from the archive of the SRK that is left over examined by the expert of the Defence for military matters which will point to the facts that General Galic planned, instigated, or approved any kind of wrong or unlawful operation. On the contrary, many documents show that General Galic ordered restraint or ordered them to refrain from undertaking any unlawful actions or operations toward civilians and civilian facilities. Relations with UNPROFOR and the system of observers of the UN were under the authority of the Main Staff of the VRS, and it was only on several occasions that this communication went through the liaison officer with the call. This is a very important question when we address -- when we look at the possibility that General Galic could be informed about some protest. And Defence will prove that General Galic, when he was informed by the Main Staff, he always undertook the necessary measures to investigate all circumstances surrounding such cases. There were many cases when the Main Staff did not address General Galic, and some contentious questions were resolved on the highest level of the VRS and UNPROFOR commands. The question of responsibility of General Galic for terrorising civilian population, as it is alleged in count 1 of the indictment, is a question which cannot be looked at in such a narrow way as it is done by the Prosecution, but is satisfied the claims of the witnesses that the citizens felt fear and by the findings of expert Dr. Turner who spoke about fear, that is terror, from the positions of theoretical musings, and that not as psychiatrist, yet he did not conduct a single psychiatric interview with a person from Sarajevo, let alone did he conduct any other methods of observation on the basis of which it will be possible to claim and to establish that this person has really felt fear which grew to be terror. Not every fear is terror. Citizens of Sarajevo living in war certainly felt fear occasionally, but this fear was certainly not of such intensity that we could call it extreme fear, which should be felt by the majority of the population in order to speak about terror. However, even the existence of fear among the majority of the population is not reason enough to claim that there was terror caused by shelling and sniping, which could be included in the incrimination given by the Prosecutor in the indictment. According to Defence, it's necessary to prove the existence of intent to use shelling or sniping to conduct terror against civilians, while the Defence will show that there was no such intent. By the very fact that civilians or civilian targets were never targeted, the intent was always to target military targets. There was no intent to terrorise civilians in this way. The Defence will, of course, in the end ask for the question of communicative charge and accusations that General Galic is being charged with. It is already now the Defence can claim that the evidence will show that General Galic cannot be held responsible for implementing terror on civilians because there was no intent to do this. The Defence will try, will endeavor, to prove through evidence that General Galic, when following an order, that he could not oppose, the position of the SRK commander, and found the initial situation which could be called a military mess. These were the first months after the VRS was established from the units of Territorial Defence, exclusively from the men who lived in this area, who were defending their land and their houses, and they were not at all on -- certainly not sufficiently military trained. That was at a time when there was no military discipline. When the command staff were not up to establishment levels and was basically reduced to reserve military personnel; they were not professionally soldiers. And through their non-military behaviour, they brought disrespect to the army. This was at the time when an obvious mixing, obvious involvement of political structures of local power in the command of military units. Basically, for General Galic as a commander of the corps he needed a lot of military knowledge and a lot of effort to eliminate all these negative occurrences. Some of them he was never able to fully eliminate, not even to the end of his mandate. Through his work, with the assistance of his associates, he still managed to bring in and implement a minimum of necessary military discipline to bring under his command paramilitary groups and to disban others while some individuals were prosecuted through the organs of military judiciary. All of this asked of -- demanded from General Galic a lot of effort when we look at the length of the front line that he held with the front of the corps with only 18.000 soldiers opposing much stronger enemy forces, which also -- there was also a difficulty regarding the control of the units, since he mostly received written reports from his units. At the end, the Defence would like to point to some facts for the Trial Chamber. In the video recording, the Defence will show in the next seven minutes, the facts will not be expressed in the words of the Defence. So in order not to be judged as subjective but in the words of those who were in some way either witnesses or participants or everything that was happening before the war, around the war, or during the war all -- they had examined, analysed the war, showing to the world under difficult light the causes of war, the causes of its many years of duration, showing the world that this war could have been avoided if the International Community had been objective and neutral. Could we please have the tape MFI-24. Your Honour, after we finish watching the tape, my colleague will take over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I take it that -- I didn't count -- but this was the passage of the video, Ms. Pilipovic, that you wanted to show, and I do understand that you take over now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President and Your Honours. The Defence would first like to thank you for the recent decision that you issued on the 3rd of October. And we can see that we think that we are going in the right direction, because this is already on three incidents that you found our client not guilty. Now, first of all, I would like to concentrate on the plan. If there was a plan in Sarajevo, it was certainly not a corps plan, and that certainly this was not a corps plan that had the objective to eliminate Muslim population. We spoke about it at length, but it doesn't seem that anything was proved. It was a plan, a campaign, that goes before April or May 1992 which consisted to organise from this day onwards the dismantling of what was a multi-ethnic Bosnia. This was a plan that was going to dismantle or cause the dismantling of multi-ethnic Bosnia in order to make a quasi-mona [phoen] ethnic Bosnia. If there was a plan, it was probably the plan of the International Community, this very same International Community which now established this Tribunal, our Tribunal, your Tribunal which is prosecuting General Galic. At that time, the community didn't care much or didn't care enough for this breakup of the former Yugoslavia, when at that time they could have just accelerated its breakup for reasons of political opportunity. Now, when we look at history, nobody could have ignored the risks. This was almost certainty of a conflict where Yugoslavia is necessarily going to be precipitated. And if there are any responsibilities, first of all, we should look at our responsibilities, and I mean the responsibility of the International Community. Now these facts, they come before the period that is in the indictment. But in order to be able to understand how and why a man, an officer that sometimes is called a man of honour, finds himself having a duty to obey in the middle of a whirlwind that he certainly -- where he didn't want to find himself and certainly didn't want to be an accomplice. When history passes, ladies and gentlemen, Your Honours, we know that it needs a little individual people. But when history has passed, when the history has unfolded, it is these same men - and since one has to justify war - who will look for the culprits. And it is usually amongst the defeated, amongst the relinquished, that one will look for them. As for law, the Judges who have been designated by the International Community are here to show, in the eyes of the Defence, that now that we have entered the 21st century, the international justice will have to see which are the things that an accused is charged of. The international justice above all and especially above any political considerations would never agree to rescind itself to some simplified applications of a syllogism. If Serb soldiers fired at a city, they were -- there were civilians in Sarajevo, therefore Serb soldiers deliberately conducted a campaign against the civilians. It sounds very simple. However, the Defence will set out to show not only that there was no plan, as is claimed by the Prosecution, but that there was even a less so any campaign. Of course, it is rather difficult to exercise because the Defence will have to show something which we know is not just what the lawyers call probatio diabolica. And that is why we should be call a number of military witnesses. Each one of these witnesses will be coming here to tell us about a part of the line to cover the particular sector. And he will show that he never had instructions, never had orders, to open fire on this or that civilian target. And we shall have to do it not to answer, but we have to do it in a very structural and systematic manner in order to show through these witness that such orders never existed. And these witnesses will have to do that. Ms. Pilipovic has mentioned how scattered were the targets in Sarajevo, and we will have to cover all of them. Therefore, we shall have a number of Defence witnesses who will be speaking to that effect; no plan, but also likewise, no besieged Sarajevo. We know that international Sarajevo in one voice presented Sarajevo as a city which was besieged from all parts. Basically by Serb attackers who were described as aggressors in the near physiology of the Presidency who were, of course, on different elevations and blindly firing at the city; and on the other side, there were the defenders of this city. There is nothing that could be more schematical than this reduced vision of the facts and nothing could be more false. And suffice it merely to remind of the figures or the statistics which the Prosecution has provided itself which never -- which that there were no -- that there was no siege and what is particularly important in the case of the Defence is to establish, Mr. President, Your Honours, how far the line -- and I am talking about the buildings which we saw a moment ago -- how these buildings which separated it into parties and how far the confrontation lines were close, were nearby, and to which extent from the point of military action, so that the military -- and what was the result of the military action as our experts will show it. While we still remember these images and while we still know, the citizens had to suffer the winter, all its rigors, and also some Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 13220 to 13228. difficulties in order to somehow find supplies to heat themselves, to find firewood or something. But we have to be very careful as to what your Chamber indirectly qualified about the exploitation of difficulties of the predicament and why the city was under siege or allegedly under siege. Well the Defence argument is: In the hospitals - and we shall prove it - there were prisons in their cellars and there were also places from which fire was opened. We shall show that Serbs were not fanatical, crazy, sharp shooters, but in this city there were some relatives which were difficult to believe, to understand, and which need to be shown. In this regard, and particularly when it comes to the shelling, the Defence will not only show that specific -- and I am talking about specific instructions, specific orders were given to target exclusively civilian targets, but also that never there were any instructions, at least that is the Defence's case, that the destruction of the urban infrastructure was rather the politics of the politicians rather than the military. And by this, I mean mostly the politics inside rather than the politics outside. We shall also establish that the forces hostile to the troops and General Galic, when they showed also committed, they too, and in a nonlegible manner, wrong, or that they also committed mistakes, that their fire also went wrong and it also provoked collateral damage. Well, if such errors were committed and considerably so, the Defence will also prove the reality of its allegation. And according to that which one has an urban war such errors and such mistakes, such damage, unfortunately is frequently possible. The Defence has never had an investigation conducted or a case opened against somebody who was responsible, whoever it might have been, in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is the Presidency for such errors or for such damages. What is the task of a military in war? The principle task of a military is to do everything, to do his utmost. Of course what is legitimately possible, to do everything within his power is to win the war, or at least not to lose it. Sarajevo was in the centre of the war. Who held Sarajevo held Bosnia, and it was also one of the theatres of operations. So the obsession of any military commander, the nightmare of any military commander is precisely this situation with which General Galic was faced. And that was the ratio between the coalition of forces. The forces of General Galic were 400 per cent larger stronger than General Galic's. It is also true that the task of a commander is also to do everything under such circumstances to reduce this imbalance, to try to strike a better balance of forces in order to avoid what we fear nothing more, because otherwise, we are talking about a battle which is lost in advance. Therefore, the first task, the principle task of a military commander is when the armies are such -- and that was the case as it was the case in Sarajevo, to try to reach those soldiers with the means that it had at its disposal, and the only way to do it is indirect fire. In reality, in the historical reality, we have very many cases when armies were dug in and were entrenched. And I believe we already heard the cases quoted of Broda and we also heard the cases in Afghanistan. Here again we have the same problem. In order to reduce the imbalance of forces and in order to somehow reach the adverse army, one has to adjust his means. And the Defence will endeavor to prove not only that it was legitimate but also that it was General Galic's duty to begin with; but also secondly, in order to be able to reach the armies which are dug in, needed a large number of shots, and that it wasn't one or two or three shells fired in order to obtain that particular military objective, and that is the striking of a balance between forces. This reality which is also the reality of a trench war in Sarajevo and this explains to a certain degree, basically, the ratio of shots fired by the two armies, because obviously General Galic and his forces were trying to reduce the imbalance of forces; whereas on the other side, and that is the Sarajevo troops, that is the Presidency troops, understood it very well, they were trying to prove both the exhaustion of -- to exhaust their means of the disposal of the other army by provoking such shots. So that we had a kind of a spiral of shelling, one provoking the other one, and the other one, of course, seeking to reduce it. And that is the reason why we shall also hear testimonies about the forced labor which was introduced by the forces of the Presidency in Sarajevo, that is the forced labour in the trench areas in order to create the trenches, to establish its defence lines, the forced labour which at times involved the Muslim population and sometimes involved the population, the Croat or the Serb population. However, in this -- and this is -- and here we come to this grey area which we also seek to understand. That is, to understand means to accept the facts, to try also to grasp them as well as one can, to read what there is to read, to hear what there is to read [as interpreted], what the media, but to -- but to examine these facts free of what we are being offered of the ideas. However, the international justice cannot really act despairingly in this process. It cannot economise discussing questions such as the traffic of weapons which was very well structured in Bosnia. It cannot also avoid to discuss the troops called Mujahedin who sewed terror amongst these soldiers and who committed also numerous abuses. And it will also be possible not to talk about the friendly shots, that is, shots that were fired by the Presidency at its own people, at its own citizens, and at its own territory. One can ask oneself if it is possible, if it is envisagible, for a head of state to take such decisions. I am sure that the -- I will -- if, for instance, I will mention that the affair enigma -- I believe nobody will contradict me. The affair enigma in the coventry, for instance, will have this case. Some had to prove the status of victims and show that the others were aggressors, but that was all within the framework of a campaign which was very well orchestrated and which was being shown every day. What is the Defence's case is that the prison of justice cannot accept any other lighting but that provided by law and by reason on the other hand. And it is that reason which can in no way not touch sufficiently upon the fact that peace was offered as of December 1992. One also cannot ask anything else but try to learn if there was no -- whether there was no campaign to properly -- to exploit truly and properly the human suffering and there is also that question. We have already had the opportunity to say on behalf of the Defence that the truth can sometimes be prisoners. But we must also say that those who shout the loudest are often the least credible, they are often lawyers. We must all be courageous enough to remove the scales from our own eyes which we ourselves have put there. And finally, if there is to be only one testimony, the Defence -- we shall be happy to mention the testimony of a person who lost one of his next of kin and who decided, therefore, to offer himself as a victim. And I believe we heard it here. And that person went there, decided to be a kind of a -- to sacrifice himself. So he went to the lines presumably dressed as a civilian, but to go to a place near the front line. Since he was a civilian who went there, he was recognisable as such, and yet even though he went to the front, he was never targeted, he was never hit. Why? Evidently because he was civilian. And I believe there are things to think about and the Defence will seek the permission to take this -- these reflections to their conclusion. Ten years have passed and it was only yesterday that in Berlin, the Defence regrets this was in Berlin at the place called the Paris [Realtime transcript read in error "Paro"] Square, the Defence is very sorry, that this is having to act just like Zolen or La Benevolencija. All of these had to be stricken in order to be part of a mechanism that would show better than any other, that the Defence will try and prove. Thank you for your attention.
